title: Limitations of Use Statements in FDA Prescribing Information: Legal Basis and Review Precedents
summary: How FDA adds, narrows, and removes Limitations of Use in drug labels: the 21 CFR 201.57 basis, guidance drafting rules, and review precedents.
body_markdown:
## Limitations of Use in FDA prescribing information: legal basis, drafting conventions, and review precedents


A "Limitations of Use" (LOU) statement sits inside Section 1, Indications and Usage. It tells prescribers where the evidence behind an approved indication stops. FDA uses it to flag reasonable concern or uncertainty about safety or effectiveness in a particular population or clinical situation. It is not meant to list every gap in the data. Review documents show the agency adding LOUs at approval, moving them in and out of other sections during labeling negotiations, and removing them once new outcome or efficacy data resolve the uncertainty. This article covers the regulatory basis, FDA's drafting framework, and the review precedents that explain each type of action.


### Key takeaways


- **The legal hook is 21 CFR 201.57.** Indications and Usage must describe limitations of usefulness and uncertainty about anticipated clinical benefit in certain situations, and Highlights must briefly note "major limitations of use"[283](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-201.57)[285](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-201.57) .
- **FDA's test is clinical relevance, not missing data.** The 2018 draft Indications and Usage guidance reserves an LOU for situations where practitioners need to know about a reasonable concern or uncertainty for safe and effective use. A population that simply was not studied generally does not qualify[406](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=406)[415](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=415) .
- **LOUs are added** for uncertain effectiveness in a subset, safety signals in an off-label or longer-duration use, class benefits the product has not shown, biomarker-negative disease, statutory scope requirements, and to head off promotion for an unapproved use[59](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=59)[193](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=193)[190](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=190)[692](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=692)[226](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=226)[183](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=183) .
- **LOUs are removed** when new data close the gap. Examples in the review records include cardiovascular-outcome LOUs on lipid-lowering drugs (Zetia, Leqvio)[577](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=577)[664](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=664) . "Reserve for limited options" language has also been removed after confirmatory trial data[539](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=539)[540](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=540) .
- **Placement is negotiated.** FDA has moved statements from Warnings and Precautions into an LOU, kept restrictions in Section 5 instead of creating an LOU, and declined LOUs proposed by its own review team[191](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=191)[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=60)[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=27)[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=28) .


### Regulatory basis


Under 21 CFR 201.57(c)(2), when the applicable conditions are met, Indications and Usage must include "a succinct description of the limitations of usefulness of the drug and any uncertainty about anticipated clinical benefits, with reference to the 'Clinical Studies' section for a discussion of the available evidence." This applies when evidence supports safety and effectiveness only in selected subgroups, or when an indication is approved on a surrogate endpoint[283](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-201.57) . If the limitation bears on dosing intervals, treatment duration, or dosage modification, the section must give a concise description and cross-reference Dosage and Administration[284](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-201.57) .


For Highlights, 21 CFR 201.57(a)(6) requires a concise statement of each indication and says "Major limitations of use (e.g., lack of effect in particular subsets of the population, or second line therapy status) must be briefly noted"[285](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-201.57) .


### FDA's drafting framework


#### Core guidance documents


Two CDER/CBER labeling guidances set out the framework:


- *Indications and Usage Section of Labeling for Human Prescription Drug and Biological Products: Content and Format* (draft, July 6, 2018)[466](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=466)[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=63)
- *Labeling for Human Prescription Drug and Biological Products: Implementing the PLR Content and Format Requirements* (final, February 25, 2013)[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=68)


The draft guidance describes an LOU as a way to clarify the scope of an approved indication when reviewers have a reasonable concern or uncertainty about the risk-benefit profile. An LOU generally discourages use in a particular population or setting. That separates it from a contraindication, which applies where risk clearly outweighs any possible benefit[406](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=406) .


#### When an LOU may be appropriate


The draft guidance identifies five circumstances:


1. **Reasonable concern or uncertainty about safety or effectiveness in a clinical situation** , including populations outside the approved age range. Where evidence supports use only in selected subgroups, an LOU may help if prescribers need to understand the concern outside the approved group. It should cross-reference Clinical Studies[407](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=407)[381](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=381) .
2. **A common use that the weight of evidence shows is ineffective** , or where benefits generally do not outweigh risks. This matters most when proven alternatives exist[408](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=408) .
3. **An important benefit shown by other drugs in the class has not been shown for this drug**[409](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=409) .
4. **Important dose, interval, duration, or dose-modification considerations** , including conditions that must be met before long-term use (for example, confirming individual response first)[410](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=410)[411](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=411) .
5. **Statutorily required scope statements.** For certain single-enantiomer products approved under FD&C Act section 505(u), the required statement that the product is not approved for a condition of use of the previously approved racemate should appear as an LOU[412](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=412) .


#### When an LOU generally should not be used


The guidance advises against using an LOU to restate a contraindication or repeat what the indication already says. An example is noting that a combination-only product is not for monotherapy. Information that defines who should receive the drug (approved subgroups, prior-therapy requirements, adjunctive use, companion tests) belongs in the indication itself. Most warnings and precautions should not be repeated as LOUs[413](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=413)[382](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=382)[90](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=90)[414](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=414) .


Lack of data in an unstudied population generally does not justify an LOU unless there is a reasonable safety or effectiveness concern. The guidance gives three examples: wild-type disease when the indication is mutation-specific, lung transplant when the indication is heart transplant, and age groups outside a vaccine's approved range[415](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=415)[386](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=386) . Short-term trials in a chronic condition likewise do not call for an LOU when long-term use raises no known concern. Trial duration belongs in Clinical Studies[416](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=416)[88](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=88) .


#### Format and wording


LOUs appear separately from the indication, under a "Limitations of Use" heading, usually without a numbered subsection. A numbered subsection may be better when one limitation covers several indications, and the format should make the scope clear[417](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=417)[418](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=418) . In Highlights, major LOUs must be noted with clear scope. Limitations that apply to every indication may be grouped under a "Limitations of Use" subheading[562](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=562)[92](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=92) .


The guidance does not prescribe one formula such as "not indicated," "not recommended," or "has not been established." Its model language is matched to what is actually known[419](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=419)[420](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=420) :


Situation Model LOU language (FDA guidance)


Age-related safety concern "In patients younger than one year of age, DRUG-X can adversely affect kidney development \[see Warnings and Precautions (5.X) and Use in Specific Populations (8.4)\]"[419](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=419)


Common use shown ineffective "Multiple clinical trials failed to establish the effectiveness of DRUG-X for the prophylaxis of migraine headaches \[see Clinical Studies (14.X)\]."[422](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=422)


Class benefit not shown "The effect of DRUG-X on cardiovascular morbidity and mortality has not been determined."[423](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=423)


Repeat-course immunogenicity "The activity of DRUG-X may be neutralized by the development of anti-drug antibodies if more than a single course of treatment is administered..."[89](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=89)


Prerequisite before long-term use "Prior to implantation of a device for chronic intrathecal infusion of DRUG-X, confirm a positive clinical response to DRUG-X in a screening phase..."[91](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=91)


Population-specific toxicity (aluminum guidance) "The use of DRUG-X for parenteral nutrition in pediatric patients less than 1 year old is not recommended due to the risk of aluminum toxicity..."[421](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=421)


#### Accelerated approval and product-area guidance


FDA's final guidance on labeling for accelerated approval products (February 4, 2019) says that once clinical benefit is verified, Indications and Usage should be revised to reflect the supported population, including any new or remaining LOUs. Statements about limitations of usefulness and continued approval should be removed or revised as appropriate[120](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=120) . If an accelerated approval indication is withdrawn, the labeling must not suggest it is still approved. FDA may require an LOU about the withdrawn use, or place the associated risks in Warnings and Precautions or Adverse Reactions[121](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=121)[122](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=122)[123](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=123) . At initial accelerated approval, the basis for approval and its endpoint limitations should immediately follow the indication rather than sit under a separate heading[124](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=124) .


Product-area guidance makes related points:


- **Biosimilars.** The 2023 draft guidance on biosimilar and interchangeable labeling calls for labeling to address any LOUs relevant to the product's indications[251](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=251) .
- **Antibacterials for unmet need (2017 guidance; 2025 Q&A).** Indications and Usage should summarize the limits of the supporting data. FDA's example restricts use to patients with limited or no alternative treatment options[252](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=252)[253](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=253) .


### Precedents: when FDA adds a Limitation of Use


Rationale category Product (application) LOU and FDA reasoning


Uncertain effectiveness in a clinical subset PEDMARK (NDA 212937, 2022) "PEDMARK may not reduce the risk of ototoxicity when administered following longer cisplatin infusions, because irreversible ototoxicity may have already occurred." FDA cited reasonable concern or uncertainty about effectiveness, and the sponsor agreed[59](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=59) .


Uncertain effectiveness (Animal Rule) TPOXX (NDA 208627, 2018) LOUs stating that effectiveness had not been determined in humans and that efficacy may be reduced in immunocompromised patients[61](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=61)[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=62) .


Limited or no data with a clinical concern NEXTSTELLIS (NDA 214154, 2021) LOU for females with obesity. Data were limited at BMI 30 to <35 kg/m², and women with BMI ≥35 kg/m² were not studied[351](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=351)[337](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=337) .


Safety signal in another use or longer duration TEMBEXA (NDA 214460, 2021) Not indicated for diseases other than smallpox. In a CMV-prevention study, all-cause mortality was 16% with brincidofovir versus 10% with placebo, and FDA weighed the potential for off-label use[222](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=222)[193](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=193)[380](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=380) .


Pediatric safety short of a contraindication LINZESS (NDA 202811, 2012) The Pediatric and Maternal Health Staff recommended "not indicated in pediatric patients" because juvenile-animal findings raised concern but might not support contraindicating use in the whole pediatric population[151](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=151)[152](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=152) .


Discouraging risky off-label use OMONTYS (NDA 202799, 2012) Limitations against use in anemia of cancer and in non-dialysis CKD, given ESA class safety concerns and limited study of peginesatide[378](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=378) .


Preventing promotion of an unapproved use VYVANSE (NDA 021977/S-037, 2015) "VYVANSE is not indicated for weight loss. The safety and effectiveness of VYVANSE for the treatment of obesity have not been established." Weight loss in the binge-eating program could prompt promotion, and a weight-loss indication carries different evidentiary requirements[182](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=182)[183](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=183) .


Class benefit not demonstrated WELCHOL (NDA 210895, 2019) Cardiovascular-outcome statement moved from Warnings and Precautions to an LOU "consistent with current labeling practices"[190](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=190)[191](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=191)[192](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=192) .


Class-wide benefit-risk uncertainty AVEED (NDA 022219/S-005, 2015) FDA recommended a class LOU stating that safety and efficacy of testosterone replacement in age-related hypogonadism had not been established, citing unknown benefit, recognized risks, and a potential cardiovascular signal[328](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=328) .


Statutory scope (505(u)) FETZIMA (NDA 204168, 2013) "FETZIMA is not approved for the management of fibromyalgia. The efficacy and safety of FETZIMA for the management of fibromyalgia have not been established." Added to meet single-enantiomer exclusivity requirements[226](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=226)[412](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=412) .


Biomarker-negative disease ZELBORAF; TAFINLAR; COTELLIC Not recommended or not indicated in BRAF wild-type melanoma. The reasons given were an unstudied population, potential tumor promotion, and consistency with the labeling of a required combination partner[692](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=692)[693](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=693)[694](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=694)[695](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=695)[697](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=697)[698](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=698) .


Unstudied serious infection sites; class consistency REZZAYO (NDA 217417, 2023) "REZZAYO has not been studied in patients with endocarditis, osteomyelitis, and meningitis due to Candida." The review notes that other echinocandin labels carry this limitation[188](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=188)[189](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=189) .


Combination-use safety LITFULO (NDA 215830, 2023) Not recommended with other JAK inhibitors, biologic immunomodulators, cyclosporine, or other potent immunosuppressants, against a background of expected JAK-class risks[329](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=329)[330](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=330) .


Combination not supported OPDIVO QVANTIG (BLA 761381, 2024) "OPDIVO QVANTIG is not indicated in combination with ipilimumab," repeated across several tumor indications. The cited records do not state the rationale[443](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=443)[445](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=445)[447](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=447) .


The rationales in these reviews match the categories in the 2018 draft guidance: subset uncertainty (PEDMARK, TPOXX), common or off-label use (VYVANSE, OMONTYS), unproven class benefit (WELCHOL, AVEED), and the statutory 505(u) statement (FETZIMA). They also show FDA using an LOU as a middle option between silence and a contraindication, as in the LINZESS pediatric discussion[152](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=152) .


### Precedents: narrowing, relocating, or declining an LOU


Labeling negotiations often turn on where a restriction belongs rather than whether it exists.


- **Highlights and FPI must match, and lack-of-indication statements belong in Section 1.** For PERFOROMIST (NDA 022007), FDA added LOU language to the full Indications and Usage section that had already been accepted in Highlights. FDA stated that limitations in Highlights must also appear in the FPI and that statements about lack of indication do not belong in Warnings and Precautions[153](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=153)[154](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=154) .
- **Moving into an LOU.** For WELCHOL, a cardiovascular-outcome statement moved from Warnings and Precautions to an LOU[191](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=191) .
- **Keeping the LOU in Section 1.** For NUEDEXTA (NDA 021879), the reviewer recommended keeping limitations material in Indications and Usage rather than moving it to Warnings and Precautions, because separating it from the indication could obscure the approved use. The reviewer also refined language distinguishing pseudobulbar affect from other emotional lability[186](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=186)[187](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=187) .
- **Using Section 5 instead of an LOU.** For TAVNEOS (NDA 214487, 2021), FDA considered an LOU against use in active or uncontrolled chronic liver disease and cirrhosis because of hepatotoxicity concerns. It then accepted placing the restriction in Warnings and Precautions[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=60) .
- **An LOU instead of a narrower indication.** For XENOVIEW (NDA 214375, 2022), FDA agreed not to restrict the indication to pre-operative evaluation for lung surgery. It added "XENOVIEW has not been evaluated for use with lung perfusion imaging" instead[184](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=184)[185](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=185) .
- **Rewriting LOU bullets.** For ARANESP (BLA 103951/S-5173, 2011), FDA replaced LOU bullets with statements that Aranesp is not indicated "In patients with cancer receiving myelosuppressive chemotherapy when the anticipated outcome is cure" and "has not been shown to improve quality of life, fatigue, or patient well-being." The related indication wording was revised to reflect the population in whom benefit had been shown[224](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=224)[225](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=225) . For VALCYTE (NDA 021304/S-007), FDA recommended aligning the section 1.3 presentation with the four-bullet Highlights format and clarifying "in other solid organ transplants"[614](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=614) .
- **An LOU declined by the review division.** For LENMELDY (BLA 125758), the CBER clinical review team proposed two LOUs: possible accelerated motor progression in early-symptomatic early-juvenile patients, and lack of effect on gallbladder disease. Office of Therapeutic Products leadership did not agree. The lack of motor benefit was described in Section 14 instead[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=27)[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=28)[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=29) .


### Precedents: when FDA removes or relaxes an LOU


#### Outcome data resolve a class-benefit LOU


The lipid-lowering class provides the clearest removal precedents:


- **ZETIA (NDA 021445/S-042, July 20, 2023).** FDA removed "The effect of ZETIA on cardiovascular morbidity and mortality has not been determined." The review cited the IMPROVE-IT cardiovascular outcomes results[577](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=577)[571](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=571) . Earlier Zetia labeling also said it had not been studied in Fredrickson Types I, III, IV, and V[662](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=662) .
- **LEQVIO (inclisiran).** FDA removed the cardiovascular morbidity and mortality LOU and simplified the indication, including dropping "maximally tolerated" before statin therapy. The review cited positive cardiovascular outcomes trials with other PCSK9 inhibitors together with inclisiran safety and effectiveness data[664](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=664)[665](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=665)[666](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=666) . As described in the review, the removal drew partly on class-level outcome evidence, which makes Leqvio an unusual case.
- **VYTORIN (NDA 021687/S-061, February 8, 2024), NEXLETOL/NEXLIZET, and ZYPITAMAG (NDA 208379/S-005, January 31, 2024).** Approval letters record LOU removal. For Zypitamag, the change was made under FDA's July 30, 2021 prior approval supplement request letter, alongside removal of "dyslipidemia" language and non-LDL-C parameters[578](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=578)[667](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=667)[658](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=658)[625](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=625)[626](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=626) . The letters do not give product-specific rationales for these removals, and the July 2021 request letter concerned indication wording broadly rather than LOUs specifically[658](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=658) .


#### New indication or efficacy data accompany removal


- **RYBELSUS (NDA 213051/S-024, October 17, 2025).** FDA approved removal of the type 1 diabetes LOU in the same supplement that added a cardiovascular risk reduction indication. The approval letter does not state a rationale for the removal[541](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=541)[542](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=542)[543](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=543) .
- **AVYCAZ (NDA 206494/S-002, June 22, 2016).** FDA approved removal of "As only limited clinical safety and efficacy data for AVYCAZ are currently available, reserve AVYCAZ for use in patients who have limited or no alternative treatment options" from the complicated intra-abdominal infection indication. The same supplement added Phase 3 cIAI data, although the letter does not expressly tie the two together[538](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=538)[539](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=539)[540](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=540) . This follows the antibacterial guidance logic that such language reflects the limits of the data available at approval[252](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=252) .


#### Conversion from accelerated approval


The accelerated approval labeling guidance expects LOU and continued-approval statements to be removed or revised once benefit is verified[120](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=120) . The approval letters cited here show this happening to the restrictive indication language rather than to a statement headed "Limitations of Use." For KEYTRUDA (BLA 125514/S-4 and S-6, December 18, 2015), FDA removed the melanoma restriction to disease progressing after ipilimumab (and a BRAF inhibitor if BRAF V600-positive), along with the continued-approval statement[722](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=722) . For ALUNBRIG (NDA 208772/S-008, May 22, 2020), FDA removed the restriction to patients who had progressed on or could not tolerate crizotinib, along with the confirmatory-trial statement[723](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=723) .


### Practical implications for labeling strategy


- **Tie every proposed LOU to a specific concern.** Reviewers ask whether prescribers need the information for safe and effective use. Proposing "not studied in X" without a clinical concern runs against the draft guidance[406](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=406)[415](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=415) .
- **Expect an LOU where the data invite off-label use.** VYVANSE, TEMBEXA, and OMONTYS show FDA adding LOUs where observed effects or class history create a foreseeable unapproved use[183](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=183)[380](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=380)[378](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=378) .
- **Class labeling cuts both ways.** Class precedent has supported adding LOUs (REZZAYO, COTELLIC, AVEED) and removing them (LEQVIO)[189](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=189)[697](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=697)[328](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=328)[664](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=664) .
- **Plan the evidence that will lift the LOU.** Removals in these records follow outcome trials (ZETIA, LEQVIO), new indication data (RYBELSUS), or confirmatory efficacy data (AVYCAZ). They are processed as prior approval or efficacy supplements, sometimes at FDA's request[577](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=577)[664](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=664)[543](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=543)[540](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=540)[626](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=626) .
- **Negotiate placement early.** Section 1 versus Section 5 versus Section 14 is a common labeling-review discussion. FDA has moved statements in both directions[191](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=191)[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=60)[186](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=186)[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=29) .


### Open questions for further research


Several follow-ups remain open. These include the specific rationale for the Rybelsus type 1 diabetes LOU removal and for the Vytorin, Nexletol/Nexlizet, and Zypitamag removals. Others are whether CDER has finalized the 2018 Indications and Usage guidance, and how LOUs are being handled for biosimilars and interchangeables relative to their reference products[543](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=543)[578](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=578)[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=63)[251](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/limitations-of-use-in-fda-prescribing-information?showSourceNumber=251) .
